column1: “Kidnapping is everywhere. Our community isn't safe.”
column2: I'm sorry; that fear is real, and the numbers back you up. Kidnapping rose last year. The government declared a security emergency, ordered mass police recruitment and has trained thousands of forest guards to go after kidnappers in the forests. State police is now close to becoming law.
column3: SBM Intelligence: 7,825 people abducted July 2025–June 2026, up 66%. Over 7,000 forest guards graduated in Dec 2025, with more approved since.

column1: “The government has no plan for insecurity.”
column2: There is a plan, though results are uneven. Since November 2025: a national security emergency, large police and military recruitment, kidnappers designated as terrorists, forest guards in the worst-hit states, and a state police amendment the President sent to the National Assembly. The test is safer communities, and we should judge it by that.
column3: Forest guards: 1,000 each approved for states such as Katsina, Kaduna and Oyo in 2026.

column2: It's closer than ever. The National Assembly passed the President's state police amendment in 2026 and sent it to the states. At least 28 state assemblies have approved it, more than the 24 needed, and lawmakers are aiming to finish by December 2026.
column3: Senate passed it on 24 June 2026, the House on 23 July 2026; sent to states on 16 September 2026.

column1: “Security only matters in the North; they've forgotten us.”
column2: Every community deserves safety. Most kidnapping victims are in the North (about 94% last year), but attacks in places like Oyo and Kwara show it's spreading, which is why forest guards are being deployed in the South-West too, and why state police matters for every state.
column3: SBM: North 93.7% of abducted persons; Zamfara the worst-hit state.

column1: What must callers never say about security?
column2: Never say kidnapping is over or falling nationally; the data shows a rise. Don't blame victims' communities. Acknowledge the fear, give one concrete action, and say results must be judged by safer communities.
